standard_prerequisites.name: Binary tree in a Steiner triple system
standard_prerequisites.statement: A family indexed by finite binary sequences whose nodes are ordered by extension and whose elements grow with the index.

standard_prerequisites.name: Products above a prescribed element
standard_prerequisites.statement: Below every decomposition of an element there are two elements above any prescribed bound.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the fact that lets the construction continue at each node.

core_obligations: Attach to every finite binary sequence an element above the prescribed element, by recursion on the height using the fact that every element lies below a product of two larger elements (source lines 848-857).

Check the two required properties at each step, namely that every node lies above the prescribed element and that a node lies above its proper predecessors, both inherited from the recursive choice (source lines 848-854).

proof_roadmap.step: Recursive construction of the nodes using the existence of products above a bound.
Verification of the two ordering properties.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 841-846: for an HF-ordering of an infinite Steiner triple system, every element a and every finite n, there is a binary tree of height n above a whose nodes increase along the extension relation. The proof (source lines 847-859) builds the tree by recursion on the height, and the step uses the earlier structural fact that below a product decomposition there are two elements above any prescribed bound, which is what makes the two branches available at every node; the two ordering properties are then read off the recursive choice. The statement records the existence of the tree and neither the recursion nor the structural input at each node.
